Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. import pandas as pd
import xgboost as xgb
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
import numpy as np

# Load data
train = pd.read_csv('/app/data/train.csv')
val = pd.read_csv('/app/data/val.csv')
test = pd.read_csv('/app/data/test.csv')

# Identify feature types
num_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('num_')]
bin_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('bin_')]
cat_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('cat_')]

X_train = train.drop(columns=['target'])
y_train = train['target']
X_val = val.drop(columns=['target'])
y_val = val['target']

# Basic preprocessing: Fill numeric NaNs with median, cat NaNs with a constant
for col in num_cols:
    X_train[col] = X_train[col].fillna(X_train[col].median())
    X_val[col] = X_val[col].fillna(X_train[col].median())
    test[col] = test[col].fillna(X_train[col].median())

for col in cat_cols:
    X_train[col] = X_train[col].fillna(-1)
    X_val[col] = X_val[col].fillna(-1)
    test[col] = test[col].fillna(-1)

# Convert categories to numeric if they aren't already
for col in cat_cols:
    X_train[col] = X_train[col].astype('category').cat.codes
    X_val[col] = X_val[col].astype('category').cat.codes
    test[col] = test[col].astype('category').cat.codes

# Train XGBoost
model = xgb.XGBClassifier(n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=6, random_state=42, tree_method='hist', device='cuda' if xgb.BSTR_VERSION else 'cpu')
model.fit(X_train, y_train, eval_set=[(X_val, y_val)], early_stopping_rounds=50, verbose=False)

# Predict
preds = model.predict_proba(test)[:, 1]

# Save predictions
preds_df = pd.DataFrame({'target': preds})
preds_df.to_csv('/app/predictions.csv', index=False)
print('Predictions saved to /app/predictions.csv')
EOF

import pandas as pd
import xgboost as xgb
import numpy as np

# Load data
train = pd.read_csv('/app/data/train.csv')
val = pd.read_csv('/app/data/val.csv')
test = pd.read_csv('/app/data/test.csv')

# Identify feature types
num_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('num_')]
cat_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('cat_')]
bin_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('bin_')]

X_train = train.drop(columns=['target'])
y_train = train['target']
X_val = val.drop(columns=['target'])
y_val = val['target']

# Handle numerical NaNs
for col in num_cols:
    median = X_train[col].median()
    X_train[col] = X_train[col].fillna(median)
    X_val[col] = X_val[col].fillna(median)
    test[col] = test[col].fillna(median)

# Handle categorical features
# To ensure consistency, we map categories based on train
for col in cat_cols:
    # Fill NaNs first
    X_train[col] = X_train[col].fillna(-1)
    X_val[col] = X_val[col].fillna(-1)
    test[col] = test[col].fillna(-1)
    
    # Create mapping
    unique_cats = X_train[col].unique()
    mapping = {cat: i for i, cat in enumerate(unique_cats)}
    
    X_train[col] = X_train[col].map(mapping).fillna(len(unique_cats)).astype(int)
    X_val[col] = X_val[col].map(mapping).fillna(len(unique_cats)).astype(int)
    test[col] = test[col].map(mapping).fillna(len(unique_cats)).astype(int)

# Train XGBoost
# We use tree_method='hist' for speed
model = xgb.XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=1000,
    learning_rate=0.05,
    max_depth=6,
    random_state=42,
    tree_method='hist',
    device='cpu'
)

# Fit with early stopping
model.fit(
    X_train, y_train,
    eval_set=[(X_val, y_val)],
    early_stopping_rounds=50,
    verbose=False
)

# Predict
preds = model.predict_proba(test)[:, 1]

# Save predictions
preds_df = pd.DataFrame({'target': preds})
preds_df.to_csv('/app/predictions.csv', index=False)
print('Predictions saved to /app/predictions.csv')
EOF
